intro: Every line of Surfing Babel (scanner, detector, calibration, website, automation) was written by Claude Code, an AI coding agent, working from short requests in a conversation. The agent read code and websites, ran experiments, wrote and ran tests, opened and merged pull requests and watched the deployments. The person directed it; the agent did the engineering. Below is how it went, including the mistakes the agent caught in its own work.

stats.label: lines of Python, JavaScript, HTML and CSS

events.title: Built the scanner, detector and site
events.request: Build a website that scans Babel's slideshow and keeps images that resemble something.
events.did: Read Babelia's slideshow JavaScript and found it simply POSTs location=N, N+1, … to babelia.cgi; the location is the seed. Wrote a direct scanner, a statistical detector and a GitHub Pages site with a scheduled GitHub Actions scan.

moments.text: Its first calibration said real Babel static scored up to 14σ. The cause: the simulation used a generic JPEG quality setting. It read Babelia's exact quantisation tables out of real frames, re-encoded the simulation with them, and real static dropped back under 3σ.
The benchmark showed a small 24 px square was found only 2 times in 5. It switched to sliding windows: 5 out of 5.

events.title: Lowered the threshold so scans actually find things
events.request: Lower the threshold so it actually finds something.
events.did: Measured how often pure static reaches each score, chose 4σ, and labelled 4–8σ finds 'anomalies' so the site stays honest that they are unusual static, not pictures.

events.title: Scan now button
events.did: Checked Babelia's CORS headers first: none, so a browser can't score frames. Built the button on GitHub's API instead, with the token kept only in the visitor's browser.

moments.text: Never put a token in the public site; status works for everyone without one.

events.title: Made it able to run forever
events.request: Keep only the top finds and store smaller images.
events.did: Projected storage would hit GitHub Pages' 1 GB limit in about 8 months. Stored 28 KB previews instead of 460 KB frames (the seed regenerates the original), kept the top 100 finds and published without git history.

events.title: Proof it works, heatmaps, share links, live strip, alerts
events.request: Add share links, a live strip, heatmaps, a proof it works and alerts.
events.did: Used Babelia's own image search to find where a drawn picture lives in the archive, then fetched it back with the scanner: 339,434σ. Real pictures live at locations about 961,760 digits long, which is why the slideshow never meets one.

moments.text: The first heatmap made plain static look structured: it was computed from downscaled JPEG previews, which no longer behave like static. It moved the computation to full-resolution frames.
Edge padding counted the same evidence twice and pushed static to 7σ; fixed so static stays under 4.5σ.

events.title: Four new tests, evidence overlays and descriptions
events.request: Make the overlay perceptible, describe each find, and add more ways to screen for anomalies.
events.did: Added contrast, angled-line, repetition and symmetry tests, per-find evidence maps with adjustable thresholds, and a generated description for every find.

moments.text: The new repetition test flagged real frames at one offset, again and again. Digging in, the agent found a fingerprint of Babelia's generator: in every frame, red at row y correlates with green 156 rows lower (and green with blue), about +10σ per frame. It documented it and excluded that offset.
Its own benchmark blended two layers of static, which secretly changed the colour histogram. It switched to per-pixel mixing so only the intended signal was tested.

events.title: Usability review
events.request: Use Nielsen's usability heuristics to critique, evaluate and update the UI.
events.did: Reviewed every screen against the 10 heuristics, rated 25 findings by severity, fixed 23 and published the review in the repository.

moments.text: A failed data load looked exactly like 'no finds yet'. Now it shows an error with a Retry button.
